name: Beast of Gévaudan
description: An animal or animals that killed roughly 100 people, mostly women and children, in the former French province of Gévaudan between 1764 and 1767. The historical case generated nationwide panic, royal hunts, and centuries of debate over its zoological identity.
origin: Former French province of Gévaudan in the Margeride Mountains of south-central France, corresponding mainly to the modern department of Lozère and parts of Haute-Loire.
